selection_contract.target_institution: Advisory Committee on Excellence in Space
selection_contract.target_universe: Federal public bodies with official representation or balance language and source-addressable authority records.
selection_contract.control_selection_reason: The NSB has an official equitable-representation selection rule and source-addressable policy, major-award, and budget-vote authority; it was not selected from inferred member identity.

sources.title: NOAA Appoints Members to New Advisory Committee on Space Commerce
supports: NOAA appointed seventeen inaugural members and described them as diverse experts representing interests across the space community.
NOAA described the committee as providing independent recommendations.
NOAA expressly stated that ACES was solely advisory and made no decisions directly affecting programs.

sources.title: NOAA Solicits Nominations for ACES Membership
supports: NOAA publicly solicited nominations for up to twenty-five members.
The notice described relevant professional fields and a two-year appointment model.
Applications after the deadline could be considered for future cycles.
does_not_support: the number or identities of applicants
selection scores, rejected nominees, conflicts or exceptions

sources.title: ACES Membership
supports: The published roster contains seventeen members and affiliations.
The charter calls for fairly balanced membership of no more than twenty-five members across professional fields.
The published terms ended August 30, 2026.
does_not_support: votes, dissents, recusals or adopted outputs

sources.title: First ACES Public Meeting — October 3, 2024
supports: ACES convened one public meeting on October 3, 2024.
The agenda included approval of subcommittee topics, chairs and members, public comments, and finalization of recommendations.
The meeting was publicly noticed and available by webinar.
does_not_support: the text, vote or agency disposition of any recommendation

sources.title: ACES subcommittee pages
supports: ACES established three subcommittees after the October 2024 meeting.
The subcommittees were tasked to research and draft recommendations on space sustainability, remote-sensing licensing, and commercial-space mission authorization.

sources.title: March 2025 Meeting
supports: A second public meeting was planned for March 5, 2025 and then canceled until further notice.
The planned agenda included three subcommittee reports and finalization of recommendations to NOAA.
does_not_support: that the subcommittee reports were delivered
the reason for cancellation beyond the published notice

sources.title: Advisory Committee on Excellence in Space
supports: ACES functioned solely in an advisory capacity and had no program-management, regulatory-development or direct program-decision authority.
The Secretary of Commerce terminated ACES effective February 28, 2025 after determining that its purposes had been fulfilled.
does_not_support: a completed output or recommendation ledger
a binding remedy or affected-party correction route

sources.publisher: U.S. National Science Foundation / National Science Board
sources.title: National Science Board
supports: The NSB establishes NSF policies and advises Congress and the President.
The NSB approves major NSF awards.
The Board has twenty-five presidentially appointed members drawn from universities and industry and multiple disciplines and geographic areas.
does_not_support: that every NSB decision is independent or correct
affected-party standing or remedy in every award

sources.publisher: U.S. National Science Foundation / National Science Board
sources.title: NSB Nomination and Appointment Process
supports: The statutory membership criteria require broad disciplinary and national representation.
The President is directed to give due regard to equitable representation of women and minority scientists and engineers.
The NSB reviews nominations and transmits recommendations to the White House.
does_not_support: a complete public applicant and rejection denominator

sources.publisher: U.S. National Science Foundation / National Science Board
sources.title: 491st National Science Board closed meeting
supports: The September 3, 2024 agenda records an NSB vote to transmit the NSF FY2026 budget submission to the Office of Management and Budget.
This is an observed exercised governance power rather than advisory participation alone.
does_not_support: the vote result from the agenda alone
demographic representation as proof of neutrality

target_chronology.event: NOAA publicly solicited nominations for ACES.
ACES convened its first public meeting and created three subcommittee workstreams.
ACES was terminated effective on this date.
The planned second meeting, including subcommittee reports and recommendation finalization, did not occur.
